summary: The lecture covers the formation and early expansion of the English East India Company (EIC) in India, detailing its three presidencies (Madras, Bombay, Bengal), key officials, territorial acquisitions, and the Company's administrative structure under the Regulating Act 1773.
points: EIC incorporated 31 Dec 1600 by Queen Elizabeth I charter with 215 investors.
Captain William Hawkins first EIC agent at Jahangir's court in 1608; failed to secure factory permission.
Sir Thomas Roe and Captain Middleton obtained first factory at Surat (1612–13).
Madras Presidency founded by Francis Day; Fort St. George built 1652 on lease from Damarla Venkatadri Nayak.
Bombay acquired via Catherine of Braganza's dowry to Charles II; transferred to EIC 1687 for £10/year; Bombay Castle built.
Bengal: Shah Shuja (subahdar) allowed Hooghly factory for ₹3,000; first agent William Hedges.
Shaista Khan captured Hooghly and Kasimbazar (1680s) after EIC attempted fortification.
Job Charnock purchased Govindapur, Sutanuti, Kalikata zamindari rights for ₹1,200 (c. 1690); Fort William built c. 1700.
Regulating Act 1773: Court of Proprietors (~125) elected 24 Court of Directors; Governor of Bengal became Governor-General of Bengal (first Warren Hastings) with 4-member executive council.
1833 Charter Act: Governor-General of Bengal redesignated Governor-General of India (first William Bentinck).

check.q: Who was the first English East India Company agent to visit the Mughal court, and in which year?
Which three villages were purchased by Job Charnock to establish the Bengal Presidency?
Under the Regulating Act 1773, who elected the Court of Directors and what was the size of the Governor-General's executive council?
opts: Court of Proprietors elected 24 Directors; council had 4 members
British Parliament elected 12 Directors; council had 6 members
Shareholders elected 24 Directors; council had 3 members
Crown appointed 24 Directors; council had 5 members
